summary:
An ARC Facilities profile, republished by FMLink, of Heather Krebs, facilities director at Fort Wayne Community School District in Indiana. The district is the largest in the state, serving roughly 28,000 students across 62 buildings and 51 schools, many more than 70 years old and in a cycle of constant renovation. A headline project is a new multi-sport outdoor stadium complex for Snider High School, whose students and marching band have shared another school's stadium since the 1970s.

Krebs holds a civil engineering degree from Purdue and worked in architecture and engineering before joining the district over a decade ago. She describes Purdue as heavily male-dominated and recalls early-career colleagues reluctant to credit her work, saying she had to build respect and rapport in a male-dominated industry. She credits a school guidance counselor and a youth group counselor who was an engineer for encouraging her path.

Her team comprises five project coordinators, two program coordinators, and two architectural technicians, and she emphasizes delegation and ownership over micromanagement. She lists seven core competencies: be organized, be aware of many moving pieces, keep thoughts straight, manage time wisely, find balance amid information onslaught, filter and delegate, and build and trust the team.

Krebs worked for 13 years with the district's executive director of operations, the previous facilities director, and succeeded him when he was promoted. She has been involved with the Indiana Association of School Business Officials and served on a neighboring district's school board, which taught patience under parent pressure. On emergencies she advises a clear path of action, rapid triage, and staying calm. She uses AI cautiously for summarizing information and drafting email replies, and values having information at her fingertips in the field. She encourages more women into FM, engineering, architecture, and construction.
